text:
Rina Patel (Employee): hi team — noticed my last paycheck had NY withholding even though i live in NJ. i was onsite in nyc for 3 days last month, could that cause tax to be pulled to NY?
Maya (People Ops): good catch. normally we withhold for primary residence unless state nexus rules apply. @Carlos can you check payrun?
Carlos (Payroll): pulling payrun 2026-04-10 for Rina (EMP-9921). payroll notes show state withholding flag: NY. taxbot flagged potential multi-state days.
taxbot: alert: employee recorded 3 in-person days in NY (2026-03-15, 2026-03-17, 2026-03-18). Policy: temporary travel < 30 days typically doesn't trigger resident withholding but employer withholding rules can vary.
Zoe (Manager): Rina was onsite for product kickoff. we logged onsite days in the team calendar, didn't realize payroll would treat that as NY.
Rina Patel (Employee): i only spend less than 10% of my workdays in ny. my NJ residency is primary. i updated my address in Workday when i moved here last year.
Carlos (Payroll): quick checklist:
1) confirm residential address in Workday (done)
2) check state withholding form on file (NJ W-4 equivalent)
3) review employer Nexus/reciprocity rules between NY & NJ for withholding
If employer used site-based withholding for those paydays, we can reclassify to NJ retroactively if appropriate.
Maya (People Ops): Rina, do you have any NY tax forms (IT-2104) submitted?
Rina Patel (Employee): no, only federal W-4 and my NJ withholding form when i started. i didn't submit any NY-specific forms.
Carlos (Payroll): sounds like this was an error at the payroll rules layer — the timecard/export flagged NY site code and our rule set defaulted to site-state when site days >0 in pay period. that's aggressive.
Maya (People Ops): ugh. we should not penalize employees for short visits. can payroll update rules and correct payrun?
Carlos (Payroll): plan:
- Submit an off-cycle reclassification for payrun 2026-04-10 to change state withholding from NY -> NJ (will adjust state tax amounts and SUI where applicable).
- Patch payroll rules: change threshold to >7 days in-state within quarter before switching residence withholding.
- Notify employees impacted this quarter and log for audit.
Zoe (Manager): thanks. Rina, if you want a small interim advance to cover any shortfall while this is resolved, let me know.
Rina Patel (Employee): appreciate it. please process the fix, and i'd like confirmation once paystub updated.
HR-onboard-bot: created case HR-3201 for reclassification request. link: https://hr.example.company/cases/HR-3201
Carlos (Payroll): off-cycle queued 2026-04-12 14:03 UTC. projection: NY withheld $72.50, expected NJ withheld $38.20 -> refund to employee $34.30. if refund < $50 we'll credit to net pay; else we'll issue separate check.
Maya (People Ops): please add note to employee record and add to quarterly payroll exceptions doc. Also update hiring/remote playbook to mention this nuance so hiring ops can flag site-heavy hires.
Carlos (Payroll): done. patched rule in sandbox; will roll to prod after next payroll window. recorded note: "Payrun 2026-04-10 reclassified NY->NJ for EMP-9921 due to primary resident verification. Off-cycle refund $34.30 processed."
taxbot: reminder scheduled: audit run for multi-state withholdings on 2026-06-01.
Rina Patel (Employee): saw updated paystub, refund posted 2026-04-13. thanks everyone! :smile:
Maya (People Ops): closing loop and adding playbook item. :white_check_mark:
